clue.text: Admitting defeat, gang returns to develop well

indicators.note: a word admitting another lets it in, so one piece sits inside the other
returns means the word for the gang is read back to front

parts.note: a mob is a gang
a loss is a defeat

explanation.surface: A beaten team regroups, sees the error of its ways and starts to flourish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admitting' reads as conceding, but it signals taking in; 'returns' sends the gang word backwards before it does so.
explanation.definitionFit: To blossom is to flower, figuratively to thrive and mature well.

clue.text: On screen, Eleanor leaves wild ponies semi-trained

parts.note: Eleanor Bron is an English film and TV actress
cos is lettuce, whose leaves are eaten

explanation.surface: A TV actress walks away from half-broken wild ponies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' is the lettuce, not departing; cos is a long-leaved lettuce.
explanation.definitionFit: Broncos are wild or only partly broken horses of the American West.

clue.text: Best possible period not quite set in stone

indicators.note: set in places one piece within the stone as a jeweller would

parts.note: opal is a gemstone

indicators.note: not quite means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: time is a period

explanation.surface: An almost fixed schedule is about as good as it gets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set in stone' looks like an idiom for fixed, but 'set in' is the insertion and 'stone' the gem; 'not quite' clips the period word.
explanation.definitionFit: Optimal means most favourable, the best achievable.

clue.text: Location reporter's visited

indicators.note: a reporter speaks, so the word is as heard

parts.note: seen, as in seen a doctor, means visited

explanation.surface: A journalist turns up at a place.
explanation.definitionFit: A scene is the place where something happens, as in the scene of a crime.

clue.text: Inept tailor made incomplete pants

indicators.note: pants is British slang for rubbish, so the letters are rearranged
incomplete drops the word's final letter

explanation.surface: A clumsy tailor botched a pair of trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pants' is the anagram signal, British slang for rubbish, though it reads as trousers. 'incomplete' cuts MADE to MAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Maladroit means clumsy and lacking skill, so inept.

clue.text: Agitator from firm's foremost US site

indicators.note: foremost asks for the leading letter of the word firm's

parts.note: a spot is a site or place

explanation.surface: A troublemaker emerges from the leading American site of some company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agitator' suggests a political stirrer, but here it is simply someone who gets agitated over trifles.
explanation.definitionFit: A fusspot is a person who frets and worries needlessly, one easily agitated.

clue.text: Rural deity first to appreciate local wildlife

parts.note: a faun is a Roman rustic god

indicators.note: first to asks for the opening letter of the word appreciate

explanation.surface: A country god is the first to admire the area's animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Fauna is the animal life of a particular region.

clue.text: Dried food, veg or apples? It's bananas!

indicators.note: bananas means crazy, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: Someone baffled whether a dried foodstuff counts as vegetable or fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bananas' looks like more fruit beside 'apples' but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Split peas are dried peas, a vegetable, halved for soups.

clue.text: Trailblazer, one plugging seaside attraction

indicators.note: plugging means filling a gap, so one piece goes inside

parts.note: a pier is a seaside amusement

explanation.surface: A trailblazing figure promotes a seaside landmark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plugging' seems to mean advertising but signals putting inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A pioneer is one who first explores or opens up new ground.

clue.text: For which Shaw wrote two articles, three on odd occasions

parts.note: the and a are the definite and indefinite articles

indicators.note: on odd occasions takes the first, third and fifth letters of the word three

explanation.surface: George Bernard Shaw wrote a couple of pieces, and three more now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: Shaw was a playwright, so he wrote for the stage.

clue.text: Market more than 50 lines after public store depleted

indicators.note: after places the two Ls behind the earlier pieces

parts.note: something out is public, known to all

indicators.note: depleted empties the word store of its insides, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty
L is the abbreviation for lines

explanation.surface: A shop sells more than fifty product lines once its stock runs low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'depleted' strips TOR from STORE, leaving SE.
explanation.definitionFit: To outsell a rival is to sell more than it, beating it in the market.

clue.text: Free places to go, one gathers, in Paris

indicators.note: gathers means one piece collects the other inside it

parts.note: une is French for one, as the words in Paris signal
loos are toilets, places to go

explanation.surface: Someone in Paris finds that public toilets there are free.
explanation.definitionFit: To unloose is to set loose or release, so to free.

clue.text: Company pressure stops workers backing charity collections

indicators.note: stops as in plugs: one letter sits stopping a gap in the other word

parts.note: men are workers
P is the physics symbol for pressure

indicators.note: backing means the word for charity is read in reverse

parts.note: aid is charity

explanation.surface: Business pressure halts workers who support a charity's fundraising collections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stops' means plugs here, not halts; 'backing' reads as supporting but turns the charity word round.
explanation.definitionFit: Compendia, plural of compendium, are collected digests or anthologies.

clue.text: UK banker first to take payment for letter

indicators.note: first to asks for the opening letter of the word take

parts.note: rent is paid to a letter, someone who lets property

explanation.surface: A British bank official takes the first payment for a letter, as in post.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'banker' in crosswords is a river, with banks; 'letter' is one who lets, not mail.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trent is a major English river, and rivers have banks.

clue.text: You're aiming to do it alone, with very little input

indicators.note: input means one piece is put into the other

parts.note: sole means alone
v is the small abbreviation for very

explanation.surface: The solver tackles this by themselves with hardly any help.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition addresses the solver directly: 'it' is the puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: Anyone attempting a crossword is trying to solve it.

clue.text: One fascinating Frenchman sent up drinking song

indicators.note: drinking means taking something in, so one piece goes inside
sent up in a down clue means the name is read upwards, reversed

parts.note: Rene is a French man's name
a chant is a song

explanation.surface: A charming Frenchman is mocked for his drinking song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' reads as mocked but reverses the name, and 'drinking' takes the song inside it; 'One fascinating' is the definition, not a description.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchanter casts spells, so he fascinates or bewitches.

clue.text: Evergreen in Eliot's verse 'withered with no trace of sun'

indicators.note: withered means twisted and shrivelled, so the letters are mixed up
with no trace of says every instance of the letter is removed

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for sun, removed twice here

explanation.surface: Quoting a line of Eliot's poetry about something withered by lack of sunlight.
explanation.walkthrough: Both Ss go from ELIOTSVERSE, leaving ELIOTVERE, which 'withered' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: The olive is an evergreen tree, keeping its leaves year round.

clue.text: Receiving jab, pub worker becomes sore

indicators.note: receiving means taking another piece inside

parts.note: an inn is a pub
a dig is a jab
an ant is a worker insect

explanation.surface: A bar employee given a vaccination ends up with a sore arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sore' means aggrieved, not aching.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sore, in the sense of resentful, is being indignant.

clue.text: Requested section authorised in dictionary

indicators.note: in places the authorised word inside the dictionary

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
licit means lawful, authorised

explanation.surface: Someone asks for a particular approved entry in a dictionary.
explanation.definitionFit: To solicit is to ask for, so solicited means requested.

clue.text: Matter raised after Mark joins service

indicators.note: after places the raised piece behind the mark

parts.note: a sign is a mark

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means read upwards, reversed

parts.note: pus is matter from a wound

explanation.surface: An issue brought up after Mark enlists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Matter' is pus, not a topic; 'raised' turns it into SUP.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign up is to enlist in the armed services.

clue.text: River creature from the south with thin bony scales

indicators.note: from the south in a down clue means read upwards, reversed

parts.note: an animal is a creature

explanation.surface: A southern river fish covered in thin bony scales.
explanation.definitionFit: Laminar means arranged in thin plates or layers, like scales.

clue.text: Nameless Russian leader's about to delay retirement

indicators.note: about means the remaining letters are turned round
nameless means the abbreviation for name, N, is dropped

parts.note: Putin is the Russian leader

explanation.surface: An anonymous Russian leader is set to postpone stepping down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nameless' drops N from PUTINS, and 'about' turns PUTIS round. 'retirement' means going to bed, not leaving office.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit up is to stay up late instead of going to bed.

clue.text: Origins of Tim Rice musical for radio

indicators.note: origins of takes the first letter of each of the next two words

parts.note: Annie is a Broadway musical

explanation.surface: Lyricist Tim Rice's early work, a musical adapted for radio.
explanation.definitionFit: A trannie is a dated British slang term for a transistor radio.

clue.text: Inclined to admonish a child found in quarry

indicators.note: found in puts these letters inside the quarry word

parts.note: prey is hunted quarry

explanation.surface: Telling off a youngster discovered in a stone quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarry' is hunted prey, not a pit.
explanation.definitionFit: Preachy describes someone given to moralising lectures.

clue.text: Instrument, one exported from African country

indicators.note: exported from means a letter is sent out of the word

parts.note: Gambia is a West African country
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A musical instrument is shipped out of a West African nation.
explanation.definitionFit: A gamba, the viola da gamba, is a bowed string instrument.

clue.text: Grand American brought back mysterious crop from tropics

indicators.note: brought back means these letters are reversed

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
US means American
arcane means mysterious

explanation.surface: A grand American returns home with a strange tropical crop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns GUS into SUG.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar cane is a tall grass grown in tropical regions for its sugar.

clue.text: Acerbic couple of kings in state

indicators.note: in places the kings inside the word for state

parts.note: to say is to state
R, for rex, and K are two abbreviations for king

explanation.surface: Two monarchs in a sharp-tongued state of affairs.
explanation.definitionFit: Sarky is British slang for sarcastic, which is cutting and acerbic.

clue.text: Surfaced from bathe, any number having sunk

indicators.note: having sunk means the letter moves lower down the word

parts.note: to rinse is to bathe in water
N stands for any number in maths

explanation.surface: Someone came up from a swim after several others went under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having sunk' moves N from the middle of RINSE to the end, giving RISEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has risen has come up, surfacing.

clue.text: Statesman partly responsible for abuse Nato received

indicators.note: partly responsible for says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A politician is partly to blame for the criticism the alliance has suffered.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of a legislature, a statesman.

clue.text: Hazardous substance from canister, unstable when temperature drops

indicators.note: unstable means the letters are rearranged
drops means a letter falls out of the word

explanation.surface: A volatile chemical in a canister becomes dangerous as it cools.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drops' removes T from CANISTER, and 'unstable' rearranges CANISER.
explanation.definitionFit: Arsenic is a notoriously poisonous element.

clue.text: Paint left large streak

parts.note: port is the left side of a ship
a ray is a broad streak of light

explanation.surface: An instruction to paint a big stripe on the left.
explanation.definitionFit: To portray is to depict, as a painter does.

clue.text: Queen once taken in by judge hides here, perhaps

indicators.note: taken in by puts the queen inside the judge's word

parts.note: to try a case is to judge it
Anne was a Queen of Great Britain

explanation.surface: A former queen fooled by a judge goes into hiding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hides' is the noun, animal skins, not the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Animal skins are cured into leather at a tannery.
